content.title: England 1-1 Uruguay LIVE commentary: Three Lions denied win by stoppage-time penalty after Ben White scores upon return
content.text: Updated: 21:53, 27 Mar 2026England kickstart their final preparations for this summer's World Cup against Uruguay at Wembley tonight.The Three Lions welcome their South American opposition before taking on Japan in their last games before the tournament.1England have been thriving under Tuchel's leadership ahead of the World CupCredit: GettyEngland vs Uruguay: talkSPORT coverageThis international friendly will take place tonight, with kick-off at Wembley Stadium scheduled for 7:45pm.talkSPORT will have live coverage of the game, with commentary coming from Jim Proudfoot and Stuart Pearce.Tune in to talkSPORT through the website via the live stream or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.Visit talkSPORT BET for all the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event.Subscribe to our talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, follow us on talkSPORT Facebook and talkSPORT X.Fans can watch the game free-to-air on ITV1 or stream via ITVX.And if the dulcet tones from messrs Pearce and Proudfoot, we had David Beckham make a special appearances on Drive earlier today...FULL TIME - England 1-1 UruguayLate drama at Wembley with Federico Valverde scoring a penalty deep into stoppage-time. Ben White is once again at the centre of things having been penalised for a late challenge on Federico Vinas inside the England box. Valverde made no mistake as he slammed the ball low and to the right of James Trafford in the England goal.Plenty to ponder for the Three Lions on a strange Friday night.GOAL! England 1-0 UruguayYou couldn't write it!The returning Ben White has opened the scoring for England upon his return to the squad.It's a first international goal for White, who poked the ball into the back of the net from practically on the goal-line following a corner on the right. White's goal comes after he was booed by some England fans when coming on earlier in the second half. Thomas Tuchel's decision to recall White may have garnered a bit more popularity now...England 0-0 UruguayA few changes made by Thomas Tuchel as we enter the final 15 minutes of the 90 at Wembley.Among those is Ben White, who was greeted with boos by some of the fans having been recalled to the squad for the first time since leaving the 2022 World Cup mid-tournament. Also coming on were Lewis Hall, Harvey Barnes and Kobbie Mainoo during that flurry of changes. At the start of the second half Adam Wharton replaced Jordan Henderson, while Dominic Calvert Lewin and Cole Palmer have also been brought on. Calvert-Lewin has had the best chance of the night, the Leeds striker heading a cross wide from less than six yards out.England 0-0 UruguayStill no goals but a feisty moment at the start of the second half with Phil Foden on the end of a robust challenge by Ronald Araujo.With the two players contesting a 50-50 ball, Araujo came flying in to get his foot in first - but he took a chunk of Foden's left foot in the process.The challenge left Foden in a heap and Thomas Tuchel was raging, with the England boss berating the fourth official.Foden has now been replaced by Cole Palmer with the Manchester City star going straight down the tunnel.Half time - England 0-0 UruguayGoalless at Wembley in what's so far been an uneventful friendly. There haven't been any clear-cut chances to speak of; the two main incidents seeing both teams lose players to injury. For England, Noni Madueke went off after receiving treatment on what appeared to be a knock to the head. Jarrod Bowen replaced him. Earlier in the match, Uruguay defender Joaquin Piquerez was stretchered off after going down following a duel with Madueke by the byline on the England right.Thomas Tuchel is able to make eight changes tonight, but he doesn't have the likes of Harry Kane to call upon. England 0-0 UruguayEarly change made by Thomas Tuchel with Noni Madueke being replaced by Jarrod Bowen. A few minutes ago, Madueke received treatment on a head injury after landing awkwardly when taking a shot. He was deemed fine to continue, however, the Arsenal winger made his way down to the ground a couple of minutes later and was brought off. It remains to be seen what the nature of Madueke's injury is. England 0-0 UruguayA worrying moment at the beginning of tonight's friendly with Uruguay's Joaquin Piquerez going off on a stretcher just now.Piquerez received treatment on what appears to be an ankle injury after a duel with England star Noni Madueke. The full-back, who plays for Brazilian club Palmeiras was down for a few minutes before being stretchered off by paramedics and Uruguay medical staff.He was subsequently replaced by Jose María Gimenez. England 0-0 UruguayWe are underway at Wembley Stadium!Last time outIt's been 12 years since England and Uruguay last played each other.It came at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, with the two sides drawn in Group D.Luis Suarez put Uruguay ahead shortly before the break, and it was Wayne Rooney who brought England level on 75 minutes.However, Suarez thumped in his second of the match in the closing stages to win it for his country,Luckily for England, the former Liverpool and Barcelona star will not be able to haunt them at Wembley Stadium tonight!'Very hard not to take'No Trent Alexander-Arnold tonight, or on Tuesday night's friendly against Japan as the Real Madrid star was omitted from this squad. However, David Beckham reckons all hope is not lost for an Alexander-Arnold call-up ahead of this summer's World Cup. "That's why I'm not England manager, because I don't have to make those decisions!" Beckham told talkSPORT when asked about Thomas Tuchel's decision to omit Alexander-Arnold."But, I'm a massive fan of Trent, I love Trent as a player. I've heard so many times over the years when he was at Liverpool, when he's at Madrid, when he's playing for England, about, 'Well, he's not as good at defending as he is (attacking)'."Well, sometimes you have to accept that... Roberto Carlos was an unbelievable defender, but he was also unbelievable going forward. He'd always go forward, and then we'd have to cover him, so those kind of things you expect."But with Trent, would I take him? I'd find it very hard not to take someone like Trent. But then Thomas, he's come out and said, I think I read it this morning, that there are other players that are ahead of him at the moment."But he said 'at the moment', so that could change. I think you said it, tonight might prove that other players are playing that might not get in the squad, so you don't know."This is very close to picking a final squad, but I still think that Thomas is probably still considering about Trent as well."Becks believesDavid Beckham believes this England team has every chance of winning the World Cup this summer.The Three Lions legend has made a special appearance on talkSPORT Drive ahead of tonight's friendly against Uruguay."I think we're in the best place that we can be, in all honesty," he said. "I think we've got a very young, talented squad with a great captain leading us in the best of form of, probably, his life with Harry (Kane)."Obviously he's a great leader, and I think Thomas is so meticulous with how he picks the squad, how he runs the squad."He's obviously had past success in the game, but I think that what he brings is how meticulous he will be with every single detail that the England team actually need to perform in this World Cup."I think the players will respond to him because he is a top manager and I think the way he handles the players, the players will respect, and I think they will react in the right way."In my opinion, he'll not be pressured into picking players that people are trying to get him to pick. He'll pick the team that he thinks will win this World Cup and I'm looking forward to it, I'm excited about it."And when asked by host Andy Goldstein later in the show if England can win the World Cup, Beckham emphatically responded: "Absolutely."Confirmed teamsThe team news is in and there's plenty of experimentation by England boss Thomas Tuchel.Tuchel has handed full senior debuts to both James Trafford and James Garner with Tottenham Hotspur striker Dominic Solanke leading the line. Meanwhile, Manchester United defender Harry Maguire comes back in and Jordan Henderson captains the side in the absence of Harry Kane.A total of 11 changes have been made from England's last fixture which saw them claim a 2-0 win over Albania in World Cup qualifying back in November.England: Trafford, Livramento, Tomori, Maguire, Spence, Henderson, Garner, Foden, Madueke, Solanke, RashfordSubs: Pickford, Hall, Wharton, Stones, Palmer, White, Ramsdale, Mainoo, Calvert-Lewin, Barnes, Bowen, SteeleUruguay: Muslera, Varela, R. Araujo, Olivera, Piquerez, Valverde, Ugarte, De Arrascaeta, Canobbio, Aguirre, M. AraujoSubs: Caceres, Fonseca, Gimenez, Martinez, Mele, Nunez, Pellistri, Rochet, J. Rodriguez, B.
